title: OpenAI 向 Pro、Enterprise 和 Business Premium 用户推出 GPT-6 Astra，消息额度约为 GPT-5.6 Sol 的一半
content:
OpenAI 已通过 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex，向所有使用 Pro、Enterprise 和 Business Premium 套餐的 ChatGPT 用户开放 GPT-6 Astra。
这款新模型也可通过 OpenAI API、Microsoft Azure 和 AWS Bedrock 访问。Plus 和 Business 用户将在未来几天内获得访问权限。Pro、Business 和 Enterprise 订阅用户还可使用 GPT-6 Astra Pro，这是该模型中功能更强的版本。Astra Pro 的使用量会计入现有订阅配额。$200 Pro 套餐每周包含 200 条 GPT-6 Pro 消息，而 $100 Pro 套餐每周包含 50 条。Business Premium 用户同样每周获得 50 条。Business Standard 用户每月仅限 15 条消息。
在所有套餐中，标准版 GPT-6 Astra 在每五小时窗口内的消息条数约为 GPT-5.6 Sol 的一半。Plus 用户使用 Astra 预计可获得 5 至 45 条本地消息，而使用 Sol 可获得 10 至 100 条。在 Pro 20x 套餐中，Astra 为 100 至 900 条，Sol 为 200 至 2,000 条。
据 OpenAI 表示，实际用量取决于模型选择、上下文长度、推理、工具使用和缓存情况。免费版和 Go 版用户无法使用前沿模型 GPT-5.6 Sol 和 GPT-6 Astra。
ChatGPT 定价
OpenAI has made GPT-6 Astra available to all ChatGPT users on Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium plans through ChatGPT Work and Codex.
The new model is also accessible through the OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock. Plus and Business users will get access in the coming days. Pro, Business, and Enterprise subscribers also get GPT-6 Astra Pro, the more capable version of the model. Astra Pro usage counts against existing subscription quotas. The $200 Pro plan includes 200 messages per week for GPT-6 Pro, while the $100 Pro plan gets 50 per week. Business Premium users also get 50 per week. Business Standard users are limited to 15 messages per month.
The standard version of GPT-6 Astra offers about half as many messages per five-hour window as GPT-5.6 Sol across all plans. Plus users get an estimated 5 to 45 local messages with Astra, compared to 10 to 100 with Sol. On the Pro 20x plan, that's 100 to 900 for Astra versus 200 to 2,000 for Sol.
Actual usage depends on model choice, context length, reasoning, tool use, and caching, according to OpenAI. Users on the Free and Go tiers don't have access to the frontier models GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.
ChatGPT Pricing

report.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra to Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium users, with lower message quotas than GPT-5.6 Sol.
report.background: OpenAI continues to roll out frontier models in staged tiers. GPT-6 Astra follows GPT-5.6 Sol as the latest high-performance system, and it is now becoming available inside ChatGPT Work and Codex rather than only in research previews. The rollout deliberately starts with expensive paid plans—Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium—then expands to Plus and Business in the coming days. Free and Go tiers will not get access to the frontier models at all. This pattern reflects OpenAI’s need to monetize heavy inference spend: new models often require more compute, so per-user message allowances are tightened to keep infrastructure costs manageable. The company also says actual message counts vary with context length, reasoning levels, tool usage, and caching. Making the model available via the OpenAI API, Azure, and AWS Bedrock signals an enterprise-focused launch, helping businesses integrate advanced capabilities while giving pros and organizations a clear upgrade path to the newest model.
key_points: GPT-6 Astra is available now to ChatGPT Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium subscribers through ChatGPT Work and Codex, with Plus and Business users getting access in the coming days. OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock also offer the model.

Subscribers on Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans also receive GPT-6 Astra Pro, a stronger version of the model. Astra Pro usage draws from the same subscription quotas: the $200 Pro plan gets 200 GPT-6 Pro messages weekly, while the $100 Pro plan gets 50 weekly.

Standard GPT-6 Astra has approximately half the message allowance per five-hour window of GPT-5.6 Sol across plans. For example, Plus users can expect about 5–45 local messages with Astra versus 10–100 with Sol, while extreme Pro 20x users see 100–900 versus 200–2,000.

Actual headline counts are estimates, and OpenAI says messaging caps depend on model selection, context length, reasoning depth, tool usage, and caching. That means heavier workflows can consume allotments far faster than simple chats.

Frontier access remains tightly gated: Free and Go tiers cannot use GPT-5.6 Sol or GPT-6 Astra. Only paid users on high-tier plans get the current frontier model today, reinforcing the idea that leading AI capabilities increasingly sit behind premium subscriptions.
report.impact: For the AI industry, GPT-6 Astra shows that model frontier progress is now tied to aggressive enterprise pricing and cloud partnerships, making API providers and big-cloud distribution central to adoption. Developers can now target this model across OpenAI, Azure, and Bedrock instead of being locked to one vendor, but rate limits are tighter than the previous generation, so they’ll need to design caching, shorter contexts, and cheaper reasoning strategies to avoid burning through quotas quickly. Regular users on Plus or Business will want to check their exact allotments, since Astra’s half-rate messages mean the most powerful features could feel scarce during long work sessions. The big takeaway: cutting-edge AI is no longer just about a breakthrough—it’s about managing cost, quota, and compute pressure every day.
report.tools: To follow or test GPT-6 Astra, watch OpenAI’s official API documentation, Azure OpenAI Service, and AWS Bedrock listings for model availability. Within OpenAI, ChatGPT Work and Codex are the main interfaces for paid subscribers. Developers should also track prompt-caching and reasoning-effort settings in the API to make the most of reduced message limits.
